title: Hardik Pandya Traded to Punjab Kings as Arshdeep Singh Joins Mumbai Indians
excerpt: The IPL formally announced on Wednesday that Mumbai Indians captain Hardik Pandya will move to Punjab Kings at a revised fee of Rs 18 crore, with Arshdeep Singh joining Mumbai at his existing Rs 18 crore fee, ahead of the November 17 retention deadline.
body:
• Mumbai Indians have traded captain Hardik Pandya to Punjab Kings in exchange for left-arm seamer Arshdeep Singh, the IPL announced on Wednesday.
  • Pandya joins Punjab at a revised fee of Rs 18 crore, up from Rs 16.35 crore at Mumbai; Arshdeep joins Mumbai at his existing fee of Rs 18 crore.
  • Punjab Kings CEO Satish Menon called Pandya's arrival "an important step" in the franchise's bid for a first IPL title.
  • Pandya publicly backed Shreyas Iyer to continue as Punjab's captain, writing "My Captain. Shreyas" in his first message after the trade.

Mumbai Indians have traded their captain, Hardik Pandya, to Punjab Kings in exchange for left-arm seamer Arshdeep Singh ahead of next year's Indian Premier League, the competition's organisers said on Wednesday, in one of the biggest player trades in the league's history.

Pandya, Mumbai's captain since 2024, joins Punjab at a revised fee of Rs 18 crore, up from the Rs 16.35 crore he earned at Mumbai, according to the IPL statement reported by Reuters. Arshdeep, who spent eight seasons with Punjab, joins Mumbai at his existing fee of Rs 18 crore and will partner Jasprit Bumrah in the five-time champions' pace attack.

What Punjab Are Buying

Pandya has won five IPL titles as a player: four with Mumbai in his two stints with the franchise, in 2015, 2017, 2019 and 2020, and one as captain of Gujarat Titans, whom he led to the title in their debut season in 2022 before returning to Mumbai as captain ahead of 2024. Punjab, by contrast, have never won the IPL; their best results are runners-up finishes in 2014 and 2025.

"We are delighted to welcome Hardik to the Punjab Kings family. He is a proven match-winner who brings tremendous experience, confidence and a winning mentality. As we enter the 20th season of the IPL, our focus remains on building a team capable of competing at the highest level and bringing the trophy home to Punjab. Hardik's arrival is an important step in that direction."

— Satish Menon, CEO, Punjab Kings

"My Captain. Shreyas"

The trade raised an immediate captaincy question, since Pandya arrives as a title-winning captain at a franchise led by Shreyas Iyer. Pandya answered it himself in his first message after the announcement: "Sat Sri Akal, Punjab. My Captain. Shreyas. My Coach. Ricky. My team. All of Punjab. I am standing behind you." The message named head coach Ricky Ponting alongside Iyer and publicly placed Pandya behind the existing leadership.

https://www.instagram.com/p/DfmZ_spnYyV/

Mumbai, for their part, posted a farewell: "Thank you Hardik for representing the Blue and Gold with passion and pride. We wish you all the best in your journey ahead."

What Happens Next

The deadline for franchises to submit their retention and release lists is November 17, with the IPL mini-auction scheduled for December 16 in Goa. The 20th season of the IPL is expected to be played from March to May next year; organisers have not announced the schedule.

For Punjab, the bet is that a proven title-winner changes a dressing room still chasing its first trophy. For Mumbai, the bet is that Arshdeep's eight seasons of new-ball and death bowling, paired with Bumrah, are worth their captain. Both bets are now official.
